checks: Classic is the default; desktop, narrow and breakpoint widths preserve one top row, working font and search controls, hit targets and formula space
Header context menu and tray callbacks both switch the same persisted preference; control identity, command search and workbook binding survive the switch without new source jobs
A tray layout change keeps an in-progress edit and the active formula field
Clear all caches returns both tabs to home, empties disk cache, preserves source bytes, and reopens the workbook with its leading-zero ID
Eight widths and four pixel ratios: core commands, tabs, command search, workbook name and formula controls fit and receive pointer input without new source tasks
At 760 px 3 commands fold into the overflow menu and still run
The 320 px overflow font picker updates the grid and retains the selection; an idle ribbon queues no more layouts over 12 frames
Resizing the bar itself, independent of the window, recomputes overflow
Each of the five tabs shows exactly its own panel
Every tab command is registered in command search; eight open their dialogs; a command on another tab brings its tab forward and anchors its menu to the button
A column menu opened from command search while folded is anchored to its visible button; Escape closes it and restores focus
Ctrl+F1 folds the bar, a tab opens it over the sheet for one command, and the choice is remembered
Keyboard browsing beyond the first sixty entries selects and opens the eightieth worksheet

environment: Windows x64, production web assets served in an isolated profile and headless Chromium; native Win32 menu constructed and queried without displaying it
